## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- A system builds the context for a call from instructions, the request, conversation history, and relevant data or tool results.
- Token budgets force choices. The system can retrieve, structure, summarize or refresh information and must account for its provenance.
- A retrieved document can contain a hostile instruction. Treat document content as data. Judge context quality by the results it produces and the errors it introduces.
- Context is what the model receives. In-context learning describes adaptation observed from that input. Context engineering organizes what the system chooses to supply.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

An answer misses a fact supposedly available through RAG. What should you check before concluding the model is incapable?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

Check whether the right document was retrieved, whether the relevant passage was present and readable in the final context, and whether its provenance justifies using it.

</details>
